mainTopic: Wine touched, moved or pressed by a גוי: a pierced barrel, pouring, carrying, and the winepress
overview: This amud discusses wine that a גוי touched, moved or pressed, and when that wine becomes forbidden. It opens by finishing רב פפא's ruling that only part of a pierced barrel's wine is forbidden. A second version moves the cutoff to the stopper. רב יימר links this to a dispute of תנאים in a משנה about a pierced barrel touched by a טבול יום. Next, רב פפא rules on pouring. Wine poured by a גוי is forbidden even into a Jew's cup, because it flows by the גוי's force. Wine poured by a Jew into a גוי's cup is permitted, unless the גוי tilts the cup. רב פפא also rules on a גוי carrying a closed wineskin, where the worry is sloshing, and an open cup, where the worry is touching. רב אשי disagrees and permits any wineskin. The amud then brings an argument about wine from a beam-press, with two versions of whether the dispute concerns direct force (כֹּחוֹ) or indirect force (כֹּחַ כֹּחוֹ). In a real case, רב יעקב מנהר פקוד forbade wine pressed by indirect force. A new story about a barrel begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The rest of the wine stays permitted
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of רב פפא's ruling: only part of the barrel's wine is forbidden, and the rest is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the rest of the wine is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes רב פפא's ruling from the end of the previous page. The wine down to the hole is forbidden, and the rest is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא holds that a גוי touching wine at a hole does not forbid the whole barrel. Only the wine down to the level of the hole is forbidden. The wine below that is untouched and stays permitted.

phrases.english: and the rest is permitted.
phrases.notes: This finishes רב פפא's ruling from the end of the previous page: the wine down to the hole is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's ruling begun on the previous page.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the wine down to the hole is forbidden; the wine below it is permitted.

steps.title: Second version: the cutoff is the stopper
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רב פפא's ruling says the wine down to the stopper is forbidden, and the rest is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say that רב פפא said: the wine down to the stopper is forbidden, and the rest is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רב פפא's ruling. In this version, the dividing line is the stopper instead of the hole.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions agree that only part of the barrel becomes forbidden. They disagree only about where the forbidden part ends. In this version it ends at the stopper.

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
Rav Pappa said:
Down to the stopper, the wine is forbidden,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the corrected wording is the word in square brackets. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: and the rest is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different version of the same ruling, with a different cutoff point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The wine down to the stopper is forbidden; the rest is permitted.

steps.title: A parallel from the תנאים: the first opinion on a pierced barrel
steps.stepSummary: רב יימר says this question matches a dispute of תנאים. The first opinion says a pierced barrel touched by a טבול יום is impure, wherever the hole is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יימר said: this is like a dispute of תנאים. A barrel that was pierced, whether on its top, its bottom, or its sides, and a טבול יום touched it, is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יימר ties רב פפא's ruling to an older argument in a משנה about a pierced barrel. This step quotes the first opinion in that משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion holds that once a טבול יום touches the wine at a hole, the wine is impure, no matter where the hole is. The location of the hole makes no difference to this view.

keyTerms.meaning: Like a dispute of the תנאים
Someone who immersed today but waits for nightfall to be fully pure

phrases.english: Rav Yeimar said: it is like a dispute of tanna'im:
A barrel that was pierced,
whether on its top or on its bottom,
or on its sides,
and a tevul yom touched it, it is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Links רב פפא's ruling to an earlier dispute among the תנאים.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's ruling about how much of a pierced barrel becomes forbidden.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in טבול יום about a pierced barrel touched by a טבול יום.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a side hole makes a difference
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says a barrel pierced on its top or bottom becomes impure, but one pierced on its side stays pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: if it was pierced on its top or bottom, it is impure. If it was pierced on its sides, it is pure on either side.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes the משנה with רבי יהודה's view, which argues with the first opinion. According to the explanation given, רב פפא's first version matches רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה treats a side hole differently. When the touch happens at a side hole, the rest of the wine is not made impure. This matches the idea that only part of the barrel is affected, like רב פפא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: From here and from there (on either side)

steps.whatToRemember: רב פפא's view that only part of the wine becomes forbidden parallels רבי יהודה, who holds that a side hole does not make the whole barrel impure.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
On its top or its bottom, it is impure;
on its sides, it is pure from here and from there.
phrases.notes: Whichever side the hole is on, the barrel's wine is not made impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole on the top or bottom makes the barrel impure; a hole on the side does not.

steps.title: A גוי pours from the barrel into a Jew's cup
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא rules that if a גוי holds the barrel and a Jew holds the cup, the wine is forbidden, because it flows by the גוי's force.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: if a גוי is at the barrel and a Jew is at the cup, the wine is forbidden. Why? Because when the wine comes, it comes by the גוי's force.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא starts a new topic: pouring wine when a גוי and a Jew each hold one of the containers. He asks for the reason himself and answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי's pouring is what moves the wine. Wine that moves by a גוי's force is treated as if he handled it, so it becomes forbidden. The Jew holding the cup does not help.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
A gentile at the barrel and a Jew at the cup:
the wine is forbidden.
What is the reason?
When it comes, it comes by the force of the gentile.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: גּוֹי אַדַּנָּא וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אַכּוּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new ruling by רב פפא on a related topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine poured by a גוי is forbidden even if a Jew holds the receiving cup, because it flows by the גוי's force.

steps.title: A Jew pours into a גוי's cup
steps.stepSummary: If a Jew pours and a גוי holds the cup, the wine is permitted. But if the גוי tilts the cup, the wine is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a Jew is at the barrel and a גוי is at the cup, the wine is permitted. But if the גוי tilts the cup to the side, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the reverse case: now the Jew is pouring. He adds one exception, when the גוי tilts the cup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the wine flows by the Jew's force, so the גוי just holding the cup does not make it forbidden. If the גוי tilts the cup, he is now actively moving the wine, and the wine becomes forbidden.

phrases.english: A Jew at the barrel and a gentile at the cup:
the wine is permitted.
But if he tilts it to the side, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: "He" is the גוי holding the cup.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The reverse of the previous case, with an added exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine poured by a Jew into a cup held by a גוי is permitted, unless the גוי tilts the cup.

steps.title: A גוי carrying a sealed wineskin
steps.stepSummary: If a גוי carries a wineskin while a Jew follows him, a full wineskin is permitted, but a partly full one is forbidden because the wine may slosh.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: a גוי carries a wineskin and a Jew walks behind him. If it is full, the wine is permitted, because it does not slosh. If it is partly empty, the wine is forbidden, because it might slosh.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a new case about a גוי carrying wine while a Jew watches him from behind. The answer depends on how full the wineskin is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wineskin is closed, so the גוי cannot touch the wine. The concern is that he shakes it. Wine that a גוי makes slosh around is forbidden, and only a partly empty wineskin lets the wine slosh.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
This gentile who carries a wineskin
while a Jew walks behind him:
If it is full, it is permitted, since it does not slosh.
If it is partly empty, it is forbidden, since perhaps it sloshes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: הַאי גּוֹי דְּדָרֵי זִיקָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new ruling by רב פפא about a גוי carrying wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full sealed wineskin carried by a גוי is permitted; a partly empty one is forbidden because of sloshing.

steps.title: A גוי carrying an open cup
steps.stepSummary: With an open cup the rule flips: a full cup is forbidden because the גוי might touch the wine, and a partly empty cup is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: A cup: if it is full, the wine is forbidden, because perhaps he touched it. If it is partly empty, the wine is permitted, because he did not touch it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes with an open cup, and the result is the opposite of the wineskin. Here the worry is touching, not sloshing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An open cup that is full lets the wine reach the rim, where the גוי's fingers might touch it. In a partly empty cup the wine stays below his hand, so there is no touching.
steps.whatToRemember: For רב פפא, each container has its own danger. A closed wineskin is a problem only if it can slosh, so a partly empty one is forbidden. An open cup is a problem only if the wine can be touched, so a full one is forbidden. (רב אשי in the next step disagrees about the wineskin.)
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Full is permitted for the wineskin but forbidden for the cup, because each container raises a different concern.

phrases.english: A cup:
If it is full, it is forbidden, since perhaps he touched it.
If it is partly empty, it is permitted, since he did not touch it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts an open cup with the sealed wineskin, giving the reverse result.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A full open cup carried by a גוי is forbidden because of possible touching; a partly empty one is permitted.

steps.title: A wineskin is always permitted
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says that a wineskin carried by a גוי is permitted whether it is full or only partly full, because shaking a wineskin is not a way of pouring a libation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: a wineskin, whether full or not full, is permitted. Why? Because this is not how people pour a libation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives his own ruling on the wineskin case. He permits it even when it is only partly full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7 the partly full wineskin was forbidden because the wine sloshes around as the גוי carries it. רב אשי says that sloshing does not matter. Wine shaking inside a closed skin is not the kind of motion used to pour wine for עבודה זרה, so it does not make the wine יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: A wineskin (a leather container for wine)
This is not the way a libation is poured

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי disagrees only about the wineskin. He says nothing about the open-cup case in Step 8, where the worry is that the גוי might touch the wine. A closed wineskin cannot be touched, so only sloshing is at issue.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says:

phrases.aramaic: זִיקָא, בֵּין מַלְיָא וּבֵין חַסִּירָא — שְׁרֵי,
phrases.english: A wineskin, whether full or not completely full, is permitted.
phrases.notes: We're back to the wineskin a גוי carries from Step 7.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
This is not the way of pouring a libation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: זִיקָא, בֵּין מַלְיָא וּבֵין חַסִּירָא — שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling in Step 7 that a partly full wineskin is forbidden.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wineskin carried by a גוי is permitted whether full or partly full, since sloshing is not a way of pouring a libation.

steps.title: Argument over a winepress pressed with a beam
steps.stepSummary: There is an argument about wine from a winepress worked with a beam. רב פפי permits it, and רב אשי (or רב שימי בר אשי) forbids it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A winepress that is pressed with a beam: רב פפי permits the wine. רב אשי, and some say רב שימי בר אשי, forbids it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case. A גוי presses grapes with a beam instead of with his feet, and two אמוראים argue about whether the wine is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גוי never touches the wine with his body, but the wine comes out because of the pressure he puts on the beam. רב פפי holds that without touching there is no problem. The other view holds that wine made to flow by the גוי's force is like wine he touched, just as in Step 5.

keyTerms.meaning: Pressed or squeezed (here, with a beam)

phrases.english: A winepress that is pressed with a beam:
Rav Pappi permits it;

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי, וְאִיתֵּימָא רַב שִׁימִי בַּר אָשֵׁי, אָסַר.
phrases.english: Rav Ashi, and some say Rav Shimi bar Ashi, forbids it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from carrying wine to a new case: producing wine by the גוי's pressing force.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפי permits wine from a beam-press worked by a גוי. רב אשי (or רב שימי בר אשי) forbids it.

steps.title: First version: they argue only about indirect force
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that wine pressed by the גוי's direct force is forbidden. The argument is only about force that comes from his force (כֹּחַ כֹּחוֹ).
steps.simpleTranslation: With his direct force, everyone agrees it is forbidden. Where they disagree is with the force of his force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down exactly where רב פפי and the other view disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of force. כֹּחוֹ is the גוי pushing directly. כֹּחַ כֹּחוֹ is a force he started that then works on its own. In this version direct force is forbidden by everyone, and the argument is only about the indirect level.

keyTerms.meaning: The force of his force, meaning indirect force he set in motion

phrases.english: With his direct force, everyone
does not disagree that it is forbidden.
Where they disagree is with the force of his force.
phrases.notes: He means a force the גוי started, which then presses the wine without him pushing directly.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכֹחוֹ, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דַּאֲסִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact scope of the argument in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Direct force is forbidden by all opinions. The argument is only about indirect force.

steps.title: Second version: they argue only about direct force
steps.stepSummary: Another version says everyone permits wine pressed by indirect force, and the argument is about direct force.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: with the force of his force, everyone agrees it is permitted. Where they disagree is with his direct force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of where the argument lies. It moves the argument one level up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version indirect force is permitted by everyone. The argument is about direct force: רב פפי permits even that, and the other view forbids it. So both versions agree that direct force is more serious than indirect force. They only differ on which level is argued about.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two versions. Version 1: direct force is forbidden by all, and they argue about indirect force. Version 2: indirect force is permitted by all, and they argue about direct force.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
With the force of his force, everyone
does not disagree that it is permitted.
Where they disagree is with his direct force.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: בְּכֹחַ כֹּחוֹ, כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּשְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing version of the scope defined in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Indirect force is permitted by all opinions. The argument is only about direct force.

steps.title: A real case: indirect force was forbidden
steps.stepSummary: In an actual case of indirect force, רב יעקב מנהר פקוד forbade the wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident with the force of his force, and רב יעקב from נהר פקוד forbade it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends the winepress topic with a real case that shows how it was ruled in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יעקב forbade wine pressed by indirect force. That fits the first version, where indirect force is under argument and can be forbidden. In the second version, everyone permits indirect force.

keyTerms.meaning: There was an incident (a real case)
רב יעקב from the town of נהר פקוד

steps.whatToRemember: Wine a גוי makes flow by his force can become forbidden even without touch. In practice רב יעקב מנהר פקוד forbade even indirect force (כֹּחַ כֹּחוֹ).
steps.whyThisMatters: This practical ruling leans toward being strict, and it supports the first version of the argument.

phrases.english: There was an incident with the force of his force,
and Rav Yaakov from Nehar Pekod forbade it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲוָה עוֹבָדָא בְּכֹחַ כֹּחוֹ, וְאָסַר רַב יַעֲקֹב מִנְּהַר פְּקוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical outcome of the argument in Steps 11 and 12.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice, wine pressed by a גוי's indirect force was forbidden by רב יעקב מנהר פקוד.

steps.title: Start of a new story about a barrel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new story about a certain barrel.
steps.whatsHappening: This is only a setup line. The גמרא is starting a new story about a barrel, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'הָהִיא חָבִיתָא' are a standard way of opening a real-life case. Only the opening words appear here, so the details and the ruling come next.

keyTerms.meaning: That certain (used to open a story)

phrases.english: There was a certain barrel

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new real-life case after the winepress topic closes.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This is only the opening of a new story.
